title: What happened by the close
text: After yesterday's big drop, stocks bounced today. The S&P 500 fund SPY rose 0.3% to $735.35, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 1.4% to $656.10. 11 of the 17 names on the list closed higher and 6 closed lower. A bounce after a sharp fall is common, but it does not tell us what happens next. Next week, watch whether prices hold these gains or give them back.

title: AI parts makers bounced the most
text: The five companies that sell parts and equipment for AI (NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv, AMD) rose about 4.9% on average. AMD jumped 11.0% and TSMC 6.3%. The four big AI companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) were almost flat, up 0.1% on average. Even after the jump, AMD is still about 32% below its 52 week high, so one good day does not erase a big drop.

title: Jobs report beat expectations
text: The government said employers added 165,000 jobs in October, and the unemployment rate was 4.1%. Analysts had expected fewer new jobs. A strong job market is good news for workers, but it can also make the Fed less willing to lower interest rates. That is why stocks can react in surprising ways to a strong report.

title: Rates are still the big worry
text: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, up from about 4.06% a year earlier. This yield is what the government pays to borrow money for 10 years. When it is high, safe bonds look more attractive, and fast growing tech stocks can look less attractive.

title: Lesson 41: What is a relief rally?
text: A relief rally is a quick jump in prices after a big fall, when people feel a little less scared. Today is a good example. After a very rough day yesterday, many stocks bounced, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 1.4%. Here is the catch. A bounce is not the same as a recovery. A stock that falls 20% needs to rise 25% just to get back to where it started. Sometimes prices keep falling after a bounce, and sometimes they keep rising. Nobody knows in advance. That is why many investors stick to a plan made on calm days instead of reacting to each big up or down day.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices are from today's close, November 6, 2026. Analyst price targets and company numbers come from free data sources and may be missing or a little old for some companies.
